newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt says leaving DAX could be problem.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt says leaving DAX could be problem.

text.p: The head of German retail group Karstadt AG said on Sunday that if the group is removed from the German DAX index of 30 blue-chip companies, it could have a negative effect on the share price.

Karstadt is very likely to be removed from the DAX index at a German bourse meeting on July 22 and replaced by the sportswear group Adidas. Karstadt would join the MDAX index of medium-sized companies.

The significance of the DAX to institutional investors means it would be regrettable were Karstadt to lose its DAX listing. Such a move, however, would not reflect on the state of the company, Walter Deuss, chief executive of Karstadt, said in an advance copy of an interview in the German news magazine Focus.
Adidas outranks Karstadt both in terms of market capitalisation and share turnover -- crucial criteria for membership of the index.
Adidas holds the 27th position among German companies in terms of market capitalisation and the 29th place in terms of sales.
Karstadt, on the other hand, held the 34th place in sales and the 44th place in capitalisation.
One of the key criteria for the bourse's ruling on the DAX make-up is the so-called 35-35 rule, which says a DAX member must be among the top 35 in Germany both in terms of sales and capitalisation.
Deuss said the group was introducing a new range of products and a change in the way articles for sale were presented.
Karstadt will be winding down its home improvements section, because these goods sell better in outlets outside the city centre.

Textiles will no longer be sold in seperate departments, but in themed areas. A pilot project for this new retail concept lifted sales by 15 percent in the group's outlet in Duisberg and in the next two to three years, all Karstadt stores will introduce the concept.
The group also intends to improve service. "In the past we have sometimes overdone job cuts," Deuss said.

Karstadt has been much in the news of late. Shares in the group surged over 100 marks last week on takeover speculation, even though the rumoured suitors, Germany's WCM AG and Dutch supermarket group Ahold NV denied they were interested in Karstadt.
There had also been calls recently for Deuss, in office since 1979, to resign. Deuss shows no sign of stepping down.
